title: Gonzales v. Great Lakes Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specification 2 was sustained. Specifications 1, 3, 4, and 5 were moot because of that ruling. The SJC reversed and annulled Gonzales’s divestiture, left him in good standing, and required no further action, while permitting future proceedings under the applicable BCO provisions.
first_summary: A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his procedural challenge because Presbytery had not made the required findings concerning habitual neglect of official functions and the cause of that neglect. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, while permitting Presbytery to pursue proper proceedings in the future.
summary: A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption and vehicle identify an appeal by Stephen Gonzales against Great Lakes Presbytery; the full SJC approved the panel opinion 15–0. Lines 13–17, 170–174 (printed pp. 555, 564).
evidence_notes.dispute: Gonzales challenged his BCO 34-10 divestiture and raised four additional procedural or related specifications. Lines 56–72 (printed p. 557).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Specification 2 was sustained; the others became moot. GLP failed to record and determine habitual neglect, its cause, and whether judicial process was necessary. The divestiture was reversed and annulled. Lines 76–168 (printed pp. 557–564).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not decide Gonzales’s qualifications or prohibit future proper proceedings. Donahoe’s concurrence disputed part of the majority’s discussion of acceptance and neglect. Lines 154–168, 178–245 (printed pp. 563–567).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated as the operative judgment. The result of SJC 2010-28 appears only in the factual history at lines 25–34 (printed pp. 555–556).

source_limits: The synopsis relies exclusively on the supplied case text. The separate concurrence is not treated as adopted reasoning.

score_reasons.decision: States the sustained specification, four moot specifications, reversal, annulment, status, and future options.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains GLP’s failure to make the findings required by BCO 34-10.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between divestiture without censure and required Chapter 31 process.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted ruling, historical prior case, and separate concurrence.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts necessary to explain the dispute, outcome, and procedural rule.

verification_notes: Rechecked the judgments and final relief at lines 76–92 and 166–168.
